title: RAW complete f76v comparative and epistemic reading: Galen II.44.4 under38 new fixed whole-form values
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED, NOT SELECTED OR SEMANTICALLY EXECUTED. Whole55-group f76v.37–41 ZL3b paragraph receives38 new independent values and five declared productions for entire owned GalenII.44.4. MOIST is reused for the guarded eye condition and the nourishment comparison; CABBAGE occurs five times; EFFECT owns nourishment and two urinary propositions. Similar drying, the eye exception, opposed nourishment axes, food-kind reason, juice/lettuce contrast and authorial urinary uncertainty are retained. Delayed reference, constituent projection, implicit comparator/disjunction and four synonym pairs are explicit costs. No496/music meanings are inherited or repaired.

section.greek: ξηραίνει μὲν οὖν ἀλλήλαιϲ παραπληϲίωϲ φακῆ τε καὶ κράμβη καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τὴν ὄψιν ἀμβλύνει, πλὴν εἰ τύχοι ποθ’ ὑγρότεροϲ ὢν παρὰ φύϲιν ὁ ϲύμπαϲ ὀφθαλμόϲ. ἀλλ’ ἡ μὲν φακῆ τροφὴν οὐκ ὀλίγην δίδωϲι τῷ ϲώματι καὶ ταύτην παχεῖάν τε καὶ μελαγχολικήν, ἡ κράμβη δὲ βραχεῖάν τε τροφὴν ἔχει καὶ ταύτην ὑγροτέραν τῆϲ φακῆϲ, ὡϲ ἂν οὐ ϲτερεὸν οὖϲα ϲιτίον, ἀλλὰ λάχανον. οὐ μὴν εὔχυμόν γ’ ἐϲτὶν ἔδεϲμα κράμβη, καθάπερ ἡ θρῖδαξ, ἀλλὰ καὶ μοχθηρὸν ἔχει καὶ δυϲώδη τὸν χυλόν. ἐπιφανὲϲ δ’ εἰϲ οὔρηϲιν οὔτ’ ἀγαθὸν οὔτε κακὸν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἀποβαῖνον εἰπεῖν ἔχω.
section.english_working_translation: Lentil soup and cabbage dry in a similar way, and because of this dull the sight, unless the whole eye should happen to be unnaturally moist. But lentil soup gives the body considerable nourishment, and that thick and melancholic, whereas cabbage has little nourishment, and that moister than lentil soup's, since it is not a solid food but a vegetable. Cabbage is not, however, a food with good juice like lettuce: it has a bad and foul-smelling juice. As for urination, I cannot state any manifest good or bad result from it.
section.translation_status: Own source-side semantic translation; not a target reading or certified modern pharmacology.

source_obligations: That drying is said to dull sight, except when the whole eye is abnormally moist; exception does not promise improved sight.
Lentil gives the body considerable nourishment, characterized as thick and melancholic.
Cabbage gives little nourishment, moister than lentil nourishment.
The explanation is cabbage being a vegetable rather than solid food.
Cabbage lacks good juice unlike lettuce; its juice is bad and foul-smelling.
The author cannot state a manifest good or bad urinary result from cabbage; uncertainty is not zero effect.

lexicon.denotation: The two specified foods have similar drying action. This compound does not supply their identities, the sight consequence or the exception.
The specified drying action is the author’s stated cause of the specified sight dulling; not an empirical or modern mechanism claim.
Dulling of the specified faculty, here sight; no additional harm or numerical degree.
Same directed relation at4 and31: dulling targets sight; nourishment is supplied to the body. No change to a causal connector at31.
Human visual faculty, distinct from a physical eye and from nourishment.
The guard removes the otherwise stated consequence from the claim’s scope; it does not assert the opposite effect when the guard holds.
The entire relevant eye; not the whole human body or just an unspecified wet surface.
The following moisture is beyond the relevant natural condition. No quantitative threshold is given.
Copular application; identical denotation at9,34,38. It does not select a new subject or change the property.

lexicon.type: attributed entity → ordered qualitative moisture attribute
lexicon.denotation: One moisture attribute at10/12: abnormal moisture of the eye and comparative moisture of nourishment. The two kinds are not numerically equated or directly compared with each other.
Resumes the two topic foods CABBAGE and LENTIL, whose explicit names appear later. This backward topic binding is an assumption, not two newly found plant names.

Generic food consequence/profile. At13 the comparison context selects the nourishment profile; at49/51 the explicit urinary predicates select urinary-effect propositions. It does not itself mean either NOURISHMENT or URINE.
Same food type at14/28/37/40/55; no new physical serving per occurrence and no assertion that distinct source comparisons involve one consumed object.

lexicon.type: ordered attribute value × same-kind value → strict comparison
lexicon.denotation: First bound comparison operand is greater than the second. Here the compared attribute is MOIST; no quantity, total effect strength or duration is silently substituted.
Introduces the second comparator supplied by the declared C02 syntax.
The nourishment profile supplied by a food, with amount, moisture and texture/humoral descriptors. Not identical to its intrinsic juice.
The lentil/lentil-soup food type in the owned working source. This is a guessed name; it does not identify a depicted botanical specimen.
Same OF relation at19 and41. In the postpositional owner convention, NOURISHMENT LENTIL OF means N(L), and CABBAGE OF at40/41 supplies the owner of the active juice profile J(C).
Exact copular synonym of qoky. At20 it predicates LITTLE of N(C), at22 VEGETABLE of C, and at53 VEGETABLE of C; syntax supplies subjects.
Little nourishment. No numerical amount or proportional effect on the eye is supplied.

lexicon.type: food → kind predicate or its nominal restriction
lexicon.denotation: Vegetable as a food kind, repeated23/46/54 for the same cabbage type. Nominal use identifies the already active vegetable C; it is not a filler or a new plant.
The vegetable/not-solid-food classification supplies the stated reason for the nourishment contrast. This does not introduce a second medical effect.
Boolean negation, here of SOLID_FOOD(C).
The source’s solid-food category, not all food. A vegetable is still a food in the declared type hierarchy.
One conjunction at27/42: vegetable plus not-solid-food classification; bad plus foul-smelling juice properties. No sequencing or comparison meaning.
Exact freely guessed synonym of qokain, retaining the same food type.
Exact freely guessed synonym of saiiin.
The human body receiving nourishment, not the cabbage’s solid body from sourceII.44.1 and not the eye alone.
Considerable nourishment, without a number. The little/much contrast concerns the same nourishment-amount dimension, not moisture.
One compound property conjunction: thick and melancholic. Both descriptors are retained; no modern chemical or psychiatric interpretation is asserted.
Exact freely guessed synonym of sshey. It negates good-juicedness at36 and the stated disjunction of reportability propositions at47.

The food has good intrinsic juice. This adjective presupposes a juice profile J(food); negation denies its GOOD quality, not the existence of juice. That internal constituent projection is an explicit cost.
Bad quality of the bound entity/profile; main C04 applies it to J(C). The lexical predicate alone does not determine owner or exclude application to a whole food.
Foul-smelling quality; main C04 applies it to the same J(C) as BAD. No medical effect follows.
The lettuce comparator named in the source; positive good-juiced contrast comes from the explicit C04 construction, not from the name itself.

The author can state a manifest result of the specified kind. Under NOT this is lack of warranted reportability, not proof of no physical effect and not an inability of every observer to know anything.
A manifest beneficial urinary consequence from the bound food. The source author’s ability to state it is separately scoped; the word does not assert it actually occurs.
A manifest harmful urinary consequence from the same bound food. This is a second compound descriptor, not an actual adverse event.

whole_paragraph_productions.name: SimilarDryingAndScopedEyeException
whole_paragraph_productions.reading: Lentil and cabbage dry similarly and for that reason dull sight, except when the whole eye is unnaturally moist.
whole_paragraph_productions.production: DRY_SIMILARLY CAUSES DULL TO SIGHT UNLESS WHOLE_EYE UNNATURALLY IS MOIST BOTH_FOODS
binding: BOTH_FOODS11 supplies the topic pair (L,C) to DRY_SIMILARLY1; the explicit names later do not introduce unrelated foods. This is backward reference to a source-assumed pair, not independent word identification.
CAUSES2 takes the drying claim1 as reason and DULL3 TO4 SIGHT5 as the consequence. TO4 fixes the faculty affected.

UNLESS6 scopes DULL3 TO4 SIGHT5, not the unconditional similar-drying characterization. WHOLE_EYE7 UNNATURALLY8 IS9 MOIST10 forms the guard ABNORMAL(MOIST(E)). IS applies the property; UNNATURALLY modifies the moisture attribution.
If the abnormal-moist-eye guard holds, this sentence does not assert DULL, NOT_DULL or IMPROVE. Absence of the usual dulling claim is not a positive sight benefit.

meaning.causal_effect: DRYING(F) is the stated reason for DULL(SIGHT(H)), F in {L,C}
meaning.guarded_case_outcome: No DULL/NOT_DULL/IMPROVE claim selected by this clause when guard holds.

whole_paragraph_productions.name: CabbageNourishmentComparisonAndFoodClassReason
whole_paragraph_productions.reading: Cabbage’s nourishment is moister than lentil’s and is little, because cabbage is a vegetable and not solid food.
whole_paragraph_productions.production: MOIST EFFECT CABBAGE MORE THAN NOURISHMENT LENTIL OF IS LITTLE IS VEGETABLE BECAUSE NOT SOLID_FOOD AND CABBAGE
binding: MOIST12 EFFECT13 CABBAGE14 names moisture of the nourishment effect N(C); MORE15 THAN16 compares it with NOURISHMENT17 LENTIL18 OF19 = N(L). The comparator’s nourishment kind supplies the explicitly assumed effect-domain binding for EFFECT13. Generic EFFECT is not globally narrowed to nourishment.
IS20 LITTLE21 resumes N(C), not L or N(L), as its subject. This is a declared topic continuation, not nearest-noun resolution.

IS22 VEGETABLE23 and NOT25 SOLID_FOOD26 are conjoined by AND27 and take the postposed CABBAGE28 as their same subject. BECAUSE24 marks this entire conjunction as the stated reason for the nourishment description. Its internal location and delayed subject are a fitted construction.

N(C) and N(L) are profiles of two food types, not one physical liquid. Strict MORE applies to moisture; LITTLE applies to nourishment amount. No greater amount or stronger clinical effect is inferred from greater moisture.

meaning.scope_limit: The qualitative source explanation is retained; no measured amount or causal law for every vegetable is invented.

whole_paragraph_productions.name: LentilNourishmentAndBodyRecipient
whole_paragraph_productions.reading: Lentil gives the body considerable nourishment, which is thick and melancholic.
whole_paragraph_productions.production: LENTIL NOURISHMENT TO BODY MUCH IS THICK_AND_MELANCHOLIC
binding: LENTIL29 NOURISHMENT30 names the same N(L) used as C02’s comparator. TO31 BODY32 fixes the human nourishment recipient H. The two food-type names qokain/okedy are deliberately synonymous.
MUCH33 and IS34 THICK_AND_MELANCHOLIC35 predicate amount and paired properties of N(L); BODY32 does not become the subject of THICK_AND_MELANCHOLIC.

The source gives the lentil description before the cabbage contrast; this target draft puts the explicit lentil description after the comparison. It retains the same referents and every claim, but does not claim source-linear wording.

meaning.amount_vs_moisture: The much/little amount contrast is separate from C02’s reversed moisture ordering.

whole_paragraph_productions.name: IntrinsicJuiceQualityAndLettuceContrast
whole_paragraph_productions.reading: Cabbage does not have good juice, unlike lettuce. The juice of this vegetable, cabbage, is bad and foul-smelling.
whole_paragraph_productions.production: NOT CABBAGE IS GOOD_JUICED CABBAGE OF AND BAD FOUL_SMELLING LETTUCE VEGETABLE
binding: NOT36 scopes CABBAGE37 IS38 GOOD_JUICED39. GOOD_JUICED is an adjective with a juice-profile argument J(food); its negation does not remove that profile.

CABBAGE40 OF41 binds the active juice profile J to the same C. AND42 combines BAD43 and FOUL_SMELLING44 for J(C). The juice argument is recovered from GOOD_JUICED39 rather than an extra unencoded JUICE word; this constituent projection is an explicit cost.

LETTUCE45 is a postposed contrast comparator. The fitted construction assigns GOOD_JUICED(T) affirmatively while denying it of C. There is no separate overt LIKE/UNLIKE token, so positive comparator polarity is an explicit new grammar assumption.

VEGETABLE46 nominally restricts the active subject C, already asserted VEGETABLE in C02. It does not silently classify lettuce, introduce a new vegetable or disappear as filler. This repeated topic characterization adds no new botanical observation.

meaning.projection_assumption: GOOD_JUICED exposes J(food) as a persistent dependent reference, with ordinary OF supplying its owner.

whole_paragraph_productions.name: ExplicitUrinaryReportabilityLimit
whole_paragraph_productions.reading: I cannot state a manifest urinary benefit or harm from this vegetable, cabbage.
whole_paragraph_productions.production: NOT CAN_STATE_MANIFEST EFFECT URINARY_BENEFIT EFFECT URINARY_HARM IS VEGETABLE CABBAGE
binding: The generic source author A is the implicit subject of CAN_STATE_MANIFEST48. EFFECT49 URINARY_BENEFIT50 and EFFECT51 URINARY_HARM52 supply two separate propositions with the same active source food C.

NOT47 has wide scope over the disjunction of the two reportability claims: neither a manifest benefit nor a manifest harm can be stated by A. The bare parallel EFFECT phrases form an implicit disjunction in this negative-report construction; no OR word is claimed.

IS53 VEGETABLE54 CABBAGE55 explicitly identifies the active source food C as that same vegetable. C owns both urinary propositions; EFFECT is not rebound to N(C) merely because the same word appeared at13. The urinary predicate words select the new effect domain.
This reports the author’s epistemic limit. It does not assert NOT_BENEFIT(C), NOT_HARM(C), NO_EFFECT(C), an actual benefit/harm, or everyone’s total ignorance.

continuous_working_reading: Lentil and cabbage dry similarly and for that reason dull sight, except when the whole eye is unnaturally moist. Cabbage’s nourishment is moister than lentil’s and is little, because cabbage is a vegetable and not solid food. Lentil gives the body considerable nourishment, which is thick and melancholic. Cabbage does not have good juice, unlike lettuce. The juice of this vegetable, cabbage, is bad and foul-smelling. I cannot state a manifest urinary benefit or harm from this vegetable, cabbage.

selected_target.reason: The first pre-ranked complete record supports a whole draft with recurring copulas, food/effect references, moisture and ownership. This is a post-inspection content fit under the recorded rule, not an independent recognition of the source.
selected_target.uncertainty: ZL3b lines37–40 are anchor-ineligible in the owned packet. All55 raw groups remain in scope; this does not certify every seam or authorize smoothing.

binding_assumptions.name: Food-type topic and backward pair reference
binding_assumptions.content: C and L are two source-topic food types. BOTH_FOODS11 denotes that declared pair before the first explicit CABBAGE14 and LENTIL18 names. The source supplies this topic; target initial names are not independently known. No one physical meal is assumed to be both cabbage and lentil.

binding_assumptions.name: Food effects as domain-indexed profiles
binding_assumptions.content: EFFECT(food,domain) has nourishment N(food) and urinary-proposition uses. C02’s explicit NOURISHMENT comparator fixes EFFECT13 as N(C); C05’s explicit urinary predicates fix its EFFECT49/51 as the corresponding urinary claims. The generic word keeps one denotation while the written domain arguments change.

binding_assumptions.name: Common moisture attribute without cross-kind numerical identity
binding_assumptions.content: MOIST applies to both eye and nourishment. UNNATURALLY modifies the eye attribution, while MORE compares N(C) with N(L). No eye/nourishment numerical comparison, shared threshold or modern chemistry is invented.

binding_assumptions.name: Narrow eye-exception scope
binding_assumptions.content: UNLESS6 qualifies the sight-dulling consequence only. Similar drying remains asserted. An abnormal-moist-eye case receives no opposite or beneficial effect from the exception.

binding_assumptions.name: Comparison orientation and sustained nourishment subject
binding_assumptions.content: C02 makes N(C) the first moisture operand and N(L) the THAN comparator. IS20 LITTLE21 resumes N(C), despite the closer mention of L. This is an explicit reference rule, not an automatic nearest-noun parser.

binding_assumptions.name: Postpositional ownership
binding_assumptions.content: NOURISHMENT LENTIL OF17–19 resolves to N(L); CABBAGE OF40–41 resolves the already active dependent juice profile J to C. OF is one ownership relation; it does not itself create a new food or change the dependent’s type.

binding_assumptions.name: Delayed subject and internal reason marker
binding_assumptions.content: In C02, CABBAGE28 supplies the common subject of IS22 VEGETABLE23 and NOT25 SOLID_FOOD26 AND27. BECAUSE24 scopes their whole conjunction as the reason for the earlier nourishment description. This discontinuous-looking construction is fitted and independently unconfirmed.

binding_assumptions.name: Nourishment recipient versus predicate subject
binding_assumptions.content: TO31 BODY32 makes the human body a recipient, while MUCH33 and THICK_AND_MELANCHOLIC35 remain properties of N(L). The body is not silently identified with the lentil food body or moisture-bearing eye.

binding_assumptions.name: Four explicit synonym pairs
binding_assumptions.content: qoky/r both IS; qokain/okedy both LENTIL; saiiin/san both NOURISHMENT; sshey/sol both NOT. These eight assignments are counted individually. No productive spelling law or phonetic relationship is proposed.

binding_assumptions.name: Composite descriptive contents
binding_assumptions.content: DRY_SIMILARLY, WHOLE_EYE, BOTH_FOODS, SOLID_FOOD, THICK_AND_MELANCHOLIC, GOOD_JUICED, CAN_STATE_MANIFEST, URINARY_BENEFIT and URINARY_HARM contain multiple semantic features. They are openly charged as nine composite values, not derived morphemes. Each still requires external arguments and supplies no complete multi-argument source assertion by itself.

binding_assumptions.name: Good-juiced adjective and constituent projection
binding_assumptions.content: GOOD_JUICED(food) exposes an intrinsic juice profile J(food). C04’s negation denies the GOOD predicate, not J’s existence; the later OF phrase owns that same J. This recovers the source’s juice noun through an unconfirmed lexical projection rather than pretending a separate JUICE token exists.

binding_assumptions.name: Implicit positive lettuce contrast
binding_assumptions.content: C04’s postposed LETTUCE45 supplies the positive GOOD_JUICED comparator, while NOT36 applies to C. No overt contrast word is present. This is a required extra construction, with shared-negative comparator scope retained as a serious alternative.

binding_assumptions.name: Repeated vegetable topic
binding_assumptions.content: VEGETABLE23/46/54 all concern C. Nominal repetitions46/54 carry the already asserted kind into the juice and urinary statements; they are not different plants, claims about lettuce, or words silently ignored.

binding_assumptions.name: Implicit negative-report disjunction
binding_assumptions.content: The two adjacent EFFECT URINARY_* phrases in C05 form alternative reportable propositions. NOT scopes CAN_STATE_MANIFEST over their disjunction, yielding lack of reportability of either. This is stronger than negating reportability of their conjunction and needs the declared grammar.

binding_assumptions.name: Implicit author and source of urinary effects
binding_assumptions.content: The author A supplies the subject of CAN_STATE_MANIFEST. The active food C, finally restated at55, owns both urinary propositions. EFFECT does not denote one identical physical result across nourishment and urinary contexts.

binding_assumptions.name: Qualitative axes and food kinds
binding_assumptions.content: Moisture, amount, thickness, melancholic quality, goodness and smell are separate attributes. VEGETABLE is a food kind distinct from SOLID_FOOD; GOOD_JUICED is applicable to both. No measured scalar levels, inference from moistness to amount or universal causal law for all vegetables is supplied.

binding_assumptions.name: Source order and historical modality
binding_assumptions.content: The target draft states the cabbage comparison before the full lentil profile, reversing those two descriptive source clauses without dropping their content. All physical/medical predicates are Galen’s source assertions; this draft does not report performed feeding, clinical success, measurements or modern medical truth.

binding_assumptions.name: Independent family and full source boundary
binding_assumptions.content: This account uses none of RAW496’s36 meanings, RAW491’s music dictionary or RAW497’s frozen extension rules. It interprets only complete II.44.4 and does not close RAW402/482’s missing all-five-section target gate. All old failures, gaps and source qualifications persist.

fitting_freedom.selection: 50 eligible whole paragraphs ranked under the written rule; first3 records inspected, rank1 fitted. No dictionary or reading was developed for ranks2/3. Prior exposure and grammar fitting remain open costs.

actual_reuse_and_distinct_consequences.same_value: MOIST is one attribute operator; IS is copular application, not a word-specific outcome lookup.
actual_reuse_and_distinct_consequences.different_bound_contexts: MOIST(eye) enters an abnormality guard that limits a sight claim; MORE(MOIST(N(C)),MOIST(N(L))) orders two nutrition profiles without changing their amount claims.
actual_reuse_and_distinct_consequences.limit: Moisture’s target identification and cross-kind attribute use are new assumptions, not two independent observations of a confirmed operator.

actual_reuse_and_distinct_consequences.same_value: The same food type C owns each named profile/proposition; generic EFFECT uses its explicit domain argument.
actual_reuse_and_distinct_consequences.different_bound_contexts: C can have little but comparatively moister nourishment and bad intrinsic juice while the author still cannot state either urinary benefit or harm. These are separate properties and epistemic claims, not contradictory values of one undifferentiated effect.
actual_reuse_and_distinct_consequences.limit: Domain/owner bindings are grammatical assumptions. Repeating a food name does not alone prove persistent physical portion identity.

actual_reuse_and_distinct_consequences.same_value: Negation, conjunction and ownership keep their same logical relations with different typed arguments.
actual_reuse_and_distinct_consequences.different_bound_contexts: NOT quality differs from NOT ability-to-state; AND joins food kinds in one reason and two juice properties in another; OF owns N(L) and J(C) without equating them.
actual_reuse_and_distinct_consequences.limit: Implicit comparator and report-disjunction scopes still need explicit productions; connective uniformity alone does not identify manuscript meaning.

serious_fixed_alternatives.prediction: For an abnormally moist eye the whole sentence withholds even the similar-drying attribution; it still does not assert improved sight.

serious_fixed_alternatives.changes: Keep GOOD_JUICED and LETTUCE denotations; include both C and T under C04’s negative predicate rather than assigning T affirmative comparator polarity.
serious_fixed_alternatives.prediction: Both cabbage and lettuce are denied good juice. This changes one complete source assertion and can remain internally coherent.
serious_fixed_alternatives.limit: The main has no overt contrast token; B12 is essential. This rival does not redefine the word LETTUCE or GOOD_JUICED.

serious_fixed_alternatives.changes: Keep values, but let NOT CAN_STATE_MANIFEST scope the conjunction of benefit and harm rather than their disjunction.
serious_fixed_alternatives.prediction: The author cannot state the combined benefit-and-harm proposition, yet might be able to state one separately.
serious_fixed_alternatives.limit: This weaker epistemic reading differs from source neither-good-nor-bad reportability. No actual effect is inferred by either scope.

serious_fixed_alternatives.changes: Keep BAD/FOUL_SMELLING general property denotations, but apply them to C instead of the constituent J(C).
serious_fixed_alternatives.prediction: The whole food is called bad and foul-smelling while the explicit intrinsic-juice property ownership is lost.
serious_fixed_alternatives.limit: This need not be physically or logically impossible and may be compatible with the source in a loose paraphrase. Exact juice attribution still distinguishes the main contract; no new empirical smell premise is added.

known_countercases_and_limits: The abnormal-eye exception does not affirm improved sight, no-dulling or cessation of the foods’ drying action.
Authorial inability to state urinary benefit or harm is not a zero-effect claim; absence of warranted report is not absence of effect.
Nourishment, intrinsic juice, human body and eye are distinct roles. No amount, moisture, smell or goodness predicate may migrate between them merely because the same food owns them.
